- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to underpredict; adjust forecast upward by 1–3% for next period.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >10% from prior peak), model often overreacts and overshoots; cap forecast at 10–15% above peak or use moving average to smooth.
- If sentiment is negative (≤0.33) and price is trending down, model often fails to recognize mean reversion; add 2–5% upward bias to counteract downward drift.
- Model consistently underestimates true price in early periods of a 30-day forecast (e.g., first 5–7 days); apply 2–4% upward bias to initial forecast points.
- When sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles, model tends to lag; align forecast with sentiment peak 1–2 days ahead, not 3–5 days.
- If sentiment is high but price is flat or declining, model often overcorrects; reduce forecast slope or apply downward bias of 1–3% to avoid over-optimism.
- For 30-day forecasts, model frequently misses late-period reversals (e.g., after 20–25 days); add 1–3% downward bias in final 5–7 days if sentiment turns negative.
